metadata.description: Comprehensive information about horse anatomy, proportions, and measurements

parts.name: Forehead
parts.description: Area between the eyes and ears
parts.function: Houses the frontal bone and sinuses
parts.anatomical_notes: Contains the frontal bone which protects the brain and forms large frontal sinuses that lighten the skull

parts.name: Poll
parts.description: Top of the head between the ears
parts.function: Important point of contact for bridle, sensitive area
parts.anatomical_notes: Contains the atlanto-occipital joint where the skull meets the first cervical vertebra

parts.name: Forelock
parts.description: Tuft of mane that falls over the forehead
parts.function: Provides protection from sun and insects
parts.anatomical_notes: Specialized long hairs that grow from the upper forehead and poll regions

parts.name: Eye
parts.description: Large, side-set eyes providing wide field of vision
parts.anatomical_notes: Horizontal pupil, third eyelid (nictitating membrane), tapetum lucidum reflecting layer enhances night vision
parts.notes: Horse eyes are the largest of any land mammal, approximately 2 inches in diameter

parts.name: Muzzle
parts.description: Nose and mouth area
parts.anatomical_notes: Highly sensitive with numerous tactile nerve endings, allows for discriminating selection of food

parts.name: Nostril
parts.description: External opening to nasal cavity
parts.function: Breathing, can flare during exercise or excitement
parts.anatomical_notes: Large, flexible openings capable of significant dilation during exercise, lined with sensory hairs

parts.name: Jaw
parts.description: Mandible and surrounding area
parts.anatomical_notes: Mandible has unique sideways grinding motion for processing fibrous plant material

parts.name: Ear
parts.description: Upright, funnel-shaped ears
parts.anatomical_notes: Cartilaginous structure with 16 muscles allowing independent rotation and precise control
parts.notes: Ears can rotate 180 degrees independently to locate sound sources

parts.name: Cheek
parts.description: Side area of face between eye and mouth
parts.function: Houses cheek teeth and muscles of mastication
parts.anatomical_notes: Contains powerful masseter muscles essential for grinding feed

parts.name: Lips
parts.description: Prehensile upper and lower lips
parts.anatomical_notes: Extremely sensitive with specialized nerve endings, particularly the upper lip for food selection

teeth.description: Specialized dental structures for herbivorous diet
teeth.formula: Adult horse: 2(I 3/3, C 0-1/0-1, P 3-4/3, M 3/3) = 36-42 teeth total

types.name: Incisors
types.location: Front of mouth, 6 upper and 6 lower
types.unique_feature: Change appearance with age, used for age estimation

types.name: Canines
types.location: Gap (interdental space) between incisors and premolars
types.function: Primarily vestigial, more developed in males
types.unique_feature: Often absent or rudimentary in mares

types.name: Wolf teeth
types.location: Just in front of first premolar
types.unique_feature: Small, often removed if they cause bitting issues

types.name: Premolars and Molars (cheek teeth)
types.location: Sides of jaws, 6 upper and 6 lower on each side
types.unique_feature: Form continuous grinding surface with enamel ridges

teeth.aging_through_teeth: Horses' ages can be estimated by examining wear patterns, cups in incisors, Galvayne's groove, and angle of incidence

parts.name: Crest
parts.description: Top line of the neck
parts.anatomical_notes: Contains nuchal ligament that passively supports the head and neck with minimal muscular effort

parts.name: Throatlatch
parts.description: Junction of the head and neck, under the jaw
parts.anatomical_notes: Houses trachea, esophagus, major blood vessels, and guttural pouches

parts.name: Jugular Groove
parts.description: Channel on side of neck where jugular vein runs
parts.anatomical_notes: Common site for intravenous injections and blood draws, contains jugular vein and carotid artery

parts.name: Mane
parts.description: Long hairs growing from the crest of the neck
parts.function: Protection from elements, insects; temperature regulation
parts.anatomical_notes: Specialized hairs that grow continuously and typically fall to one side

vertebrae.description: Seven cervical vertebrae form the bony structure of the neck
features: Remaining five vertebrae allow for flexibility and reach

parts.name: Withers
parts.description: Ridge between shoulder blades where neck meets back
parts.function: Anchor for muscles, height measurement point
parts.anatomical_notes: Formed by the dorsal spinous processes of approximately 5th-9th thoracic vertebrae, attachment point for many muscles
parts.notes: Used as the standard measuring point for horse height

parts.name: Back
parts.description: Area from withers to loin
parts.function: Supports rider weight, connects front and hind end
parts.anatomical_notes: Made up of thoracic vertebrae (typically T9-T18) with relatively inflexible joints due to interlocking processes

parts.name: Loin
parts.description: Short area between back and croup
parts.anatomical_notes: Corresponds to lumbar vertebrae (typically 6), lacks rib support making it vulnerable to injury

parts.name: Croup
parts.description: Top line from loin to tail
parts.anatomical_notes: Formed by sacrum and surrounding musculature, transmits propulsive force from hindlimbs

parts.name: Barrel
parts.description: Body area containing ribs and organs
parts.function: Houses vital organs like lungs and digestive system
parts.anatomical_notes: Supported by 18 pairs of ribs (8 true ribs attached to sternum, 10 floating ribs), houses heart, lungs, and digestive organs

parts.name: Flank
parts.description: Area between last rib and hip
parts.anatomical_notes: Thin-walled area with primarily abdominal muscles, site for observing respiratory rate

parts.name: Shoulder
parts.description: Area from withers to point of shoulder
parts.function: Attachment for front limb, affects stride length
parts.anatomical_notes: Contains scapula (shoulder blade) which is attached to trunk only by muscles, no bony connection to spine, allowing shock absorption

parts.name: Chest
parts.description: Area between forelegs and up to shoulder
parts.function: Houses heart and major blood vessels
parts.anatomical_notes: Protected by sternum and rib cage, width varies significantly between breeds affecting athletic capacity

parts.name: Girth
parts.description: Area behind forelegs where saddle girth goes
parts.anatomical_notes: Contains intercostal muscles between ribs, area expands and contracts during breathing

parts.name: Sternum
parts.description: Breastbone at the bottom of the chest
parts.function: Attachment point for ribs, protection for heart
parts.anatomical_notes: Flat bone that forms the ventral portion of the thoracic cavity

parts.name: Underline
parts.description: Ventral line of the body from elbow to flank
parts.anatomical_notes: Made up of abdominal muscles and connective tissue, slope varies with condition and fitness

parts.name: Hip
parts.description: Point of hip bone (tuber coxae)
parts.anatomical_notes: Visible prominence of the ilium (part of pelvis), attachment point for multiple muscle groups

parts.name: Stifle
parts.description: Joint equivalent to human knee
parts.anatomical_notes: Complex joint where femur, tibia and patella meet, contains elaborate ligament structure similar to human knee

parts.name: Gaskin
parts.description: Area between stifle and hock
parts.function: Contains muscles that flex the hock
parts.anatomical_notes: Contains tibia and fibula bones, site of powerful muscle groups that drive forward motion

parts.name: Hock
parts.description: Large joint in hind leg, equivalent to human ankle
parts.function: Absorbs shock, translates power from hindquarters
parts.anatomical_notes: Complex of 6 tarsal bones and multiple joints, critical for propulsion and susceptible to stress injuries

parts.name: Buttock
parts.description: Muscular area behind hip
parts.anatomical_notes: Contains powerful gluteal muscles that are primary drivers for propulsion

parts.name: Dock
parts.description: Base of the tail
parts.anatomical_notes: Contains coccygeal vertebrae (15-21 small bones) that decrease in size toward the tail end

parts.name: Point of Buttock
parts.description: Rearmost point of the pelvis (ischial tuberosity)
parts.anatomical_notes: Important landmark for evaluating hindquarter conformation

parts.name: Thigh
parts.description: Area from hip to stifle
parts.anatomical_notes: Contains femur bone and surrounding musculature, primary force generation for forward movement

pelvis.description: Bony structure forming foundation of hindquarters
pelvis.function: Transfers force from hindlimbs to spine, protects reproductive organs

forelegs.name: Point of Shoulder
forelegs.description: Junction of shoulder and upper arm
forelegs.anatomical_notes: Joint between scapula and humerus (shoulder joint), capable of wide range of motion

forelegs.name: Elbow
forelegs.description: Point at back of upper foreleg
forelegs.function: Joint between upper and lower foreleg
forelegs.anatomical_notes: Joint between humerus and radius/ulna, extends and flexes during movement

forelegs.name: Forearm
forelegs.anatomical_notes: Contains radius and ulna bones, ulna is fused to radius in mature horses

forelegs.name: Knee
forelegs.description: Joint between forearm and cannon bone (carpus)
forelegs.anatomical_notes: Complex joint containing 7-8 carpal bones arranged in two rows, similar to human wrist

forelegs.name: Cannon
forelegs.anatomical_notes: Contains large metacarpal bone (cannon) and two small metacarpal bones (splints) with minimal soft tissue covering

forelegs.name: Fetlock
forelegs.anatomical_notes: Equivalent to human knuckle, contains sesamoid bones at back of joint and suspensory apparatus for support

forelegs.name: Pastern
forelegs.anatomical_notes: Contains proximal and distal phalanx bones, angle has significant impact on soundness

forelegs.name: Coronet
forelegs.anatomical_notes: Contains coronary band which produces the hoof wall, analogous to human nail bed

forelegs.name: Ergot
forelegs.description: Small callous-like structure on back of fetlock
forelegs.function: Vestigial structure, remnant of ancestral toe
forelegs.anatomical_notes: Varies in size between individuals and breeds

forelegs.name: Chestnut
forelegs.description: Horny growth on inside of legs
forelegs.function: Vestigial structure, possibly remnant of scent gland
forelegs.anatomical_notes: Located above knee on forelegs, below hock on hindlegs

forelegs.name: Hoof
forelegs.description: Keratinized structure at the end of each leg
forelegs.anatomical_notes: Complex structure containing coffin bone (distal phalanx), navicular bone, and sensitive laminae

sections.name: Wall
sections.function: Primary weight-bearing structure, grows downward from coronary band

sections.name: Frog
sections.description: V-shaped structure on bottom of hoof

sections.name: Bars
sections.description: Inward folds of the wall at the heel

sections.name: White Line
sections.function: Indicates where sensitive and insensitive tissues meet

hindlegs.name: Thigh
hindlegs.description: Upper part of hindleg from hip to stifle
hindlegs.anatomical_notes: Contains femur bone and large muscle groups including quadriceps and hamstring equivalents

hindlegs.name: Gaskin
hindlegs.anatomical_notes: Contains tibia and fibula (the latter being much reduced in horses)

hindlegs.name: Hock
hindlegs.anatomical_notes: Complex joint with 6 tarsal bones, site of conditions like bone spavin and curb

hindlegs.name: Cannon
hindlegs.anatomical_notes: Contains large metatarsal bone and two small splint bones

comparative_anatomy.description: Horses walk on the tip of what corresponds to the third finger/toe
comparative_anatomy.evolution: Modern horse leg evolved from five-toed ancestor through progressive reduction
comparative_anatomy.forelimb_comparison: Elbow = human elbow, Knee = human wrist, Fetlock = knuckle of middle finger
comparative_anatomy.hindlimb_comparison: Stifle = human knee, Hock = human ankle, Fetlock = knuckle of middle toe

parts.name: Dock
parts.description: Base of the tail
parts.anatomical_notes: Contains coccygeal vertebrae and surrounding musculature

parts.name: Skirt
parts.description: Long hairs of the tail
parts.anatomical_notes: Specialized long guard hairs that grow continuously

tail.muscles: Contains coccygeal muscles that allow raising, lowering, and side-to-side movement

skeletal_system.description: The framework that supports the horse's body

components.name: Skull
components.function: Protects brain, houses sense organs, supports jaw

components.name: Vertebral Column
components.bone_count: 54 vertebrae (7 cervical, 18 thoracic, 6 lumbar, 5 sacral, 15-25 caudal)
components.function: Protects spinal cord, supports head and body
special_features: Nuchal ligament runs from poll to withers, supports head
Spinous processes at withers can reach 8-10 inches in height
Interlocking processes limit twisting but allow flexibility

components.name: Ribs
components.function: Protect thoracic organs, assist in breathing

types.name: False ribs (asternal)
types.description: Connect to cartilage of preceding ribs

major_bones.name: Scapula
major_bones.description: Shoulder blade, attached to body only by muscles
major_bones.unique_feature: No direct bony connection to spine, allows shock absorption

major_bones.name: Humerus
major_bones.description: Upper arm bone connecting shoulder to elbow

major_bones.name: Radius/Ulna
major_bones.description: Forearm bones, ulna is reduced and fused to radius in adults

major_bones.name: Carpals
major_bones.description: Seven or eight small bones forming the knee joint

major_bones.name: Metacarpals
major_bones.description: One large cannon bone and two splint bones

major_bones.name: Phalanges
major_bones.description: Three bones forming the finger (long pastern, short pastern, coffin bone)

major_bones.name: Sesamoids
major_bones.description: Small bones at back of fetlock and within the hoof (navicular)

major_bones.name: Pelvis
major_bones.description: Large bone structure connecting spine to hindlimbs

major_bones.name: Femur
major_bones.description: Thigh bone, largest bone in the body

major_bones.name: Tibia/Fibula
major_bones.description: Lower leg bones, fibula is reduced in horses

major_bones.name: Tarsals
major_bones.description: Six small bones forming the hock joint

major_bones.name: Metatarsals
major_bones.description: One large cannon bone and two splint bones

major_bones.name: Phalanges
major_bones.description: Three bones forming the toe (same as foreleg)

joints.name: Plane Joints
locations: Between some carpal and tarsal bones

muscular_system.description: System responsible for movement, posture, and heat production

major_muscle_groups.name: Neck Muscles
major_muscle_groups.function: Move head and neck, important for balance

key_muscles.name: Splenius
key_muscles.function: Raises and extends the head and neck

key_muscles.name: Brachiocephalicus
key_muscles.function: Pulls limb forward or pulls head to the side

key_muscles.name: Trapezius
key_muscles.function: Lifts and draws shoulder blade forward

key_muscles.name: Infraspinatus
key_muscles.function: Flexion and outward rotation of shoulder

key_muscles.name: Triceps brachii
key_muscles.function: Extends elbow, primary support for body weight

key_muscles.name: Longissimus dorsi
key_muscles.function: Main extensor of back, largest muscle in the body

key_muscles.name: Latissimus dorsi
key_muscles.function: Pulls front leg backward, assists respiration

major_muscle_groups.name: Abdominal Muscles
major_muscle_groups.function: Support internal organs, flex spine, assist respiration

key_muscles.name: Semitendinosus
key_muscles.function: Extends hip, flexes stifle, part of 'hamstring' group

key_muscles.name: Semimembranosus
key_muscles.function: Extends hip and stifle, part of 'hamstring' group

key_muscles.name: Biceps femoris
key_muscles.function: Largest muscle of hindquarter, extends hip and hock

key_muscles.name: Quadriceps femoris
key_muscles.function: Extends stifle, includes four divisions (rectus femoris, vastus lateralis, vastus medialis, vastus intermedius)

major_muscle_groups.name: Lower Leg Muscles

key_muscles.name: Digital extensor
key_muscles.function: Extends the pastern and coffin joints

key_muscles.name: Digital flexor
key_muscles.function: Flexes the pastern and coffin joints

major_muscle_groups.notes: Lower limbs have minimal muscle tissue, mostly tendons and ligaments

specialized_structures.name: Stay Apparatus
specialized_structures.description: Passive support system allowing horses to stand with minimal muscle exertion
specialized_structures.function: Enables horses to sleep standing up and stand for long periods with minimal fatigue

specialized_structures.name: Suspensory Apparatus
specialized_structures.function: Prevents excessive fetlock descent under weight, acts as shock absorber

height.description: Measured from ground to withers, traditionally in 'hands' (4 inches each)
height.measurement_technique: Stand horse on level ground, measure vertical distance from ground to highest point of withers

world_records.tallest: Big Jake, a Belgian gelding, 20.2 hands (82 inches, 210 cm)
world_records.shortest: Thumbelina, a miniature horse, 4.25 hands (17 inches, 44.5 cm)

weight.description: Total body mass, usually measured in pounds or kilograms

estimation_formula.standard: Heart girth (in) × heart girth (in) × body length (in) ÷ 300 = approximate weight in pounds
estimation_formula.metric: Heart girth (cm) × heart girth (cm) × body length (cm) ÷ 11,877 = approximate weight in kg

proportions.description: Ideal proportional relationships between body parts
key_ratios: Square frame: body length equals height at withers
Head length roughly equal to neck length
Shoulder angle ideally 45-50 degrees from vertical

breed_variations.thoroughbreds: Generally longer than tall, rectangular frame
breed_variations.draft_horses: More compact, broad, with shorter legs relative to body depth

balance_points: Center of gravity located near girth area, behind elbow
Lower in young horses, moves forward as neck length and head position change with maturity

key_angles.significance: Affects power transmission, susceptibility to strain

digestive.description: Specialized for processing fibrous plant material
key_features: Large cecum for fermentation (7-8 gallons/26-30 liters)
Unable to vomit due to strong cardiac sphincter

components.name: Mouth
components.special_features: Gap between incisors and cheek teeth (bars), highly mobile lips

components.name: Esophagus
components.special_features: Strong one-way movement, horses cannot vomit normally

components.name: Stomach
components.special_features: Relatively small for body size, fills continuously

components.name: Small Intestine
components.special_features: Very long (70 feet/21 meters), digestion of proteins, fats, soluble carbohydrates

components.name: Cecum
components.special_features: Large fermentation vat containing beneficial bacteria and protozoa

components.name: Large Colon
components.special_features: Complex arrangement with four parts, site of colic problems

components.name: Small Colon
components.function: Final water absorption, fecal ball formation
components.special_features: Forms characteristic fecal balls

components.name: Rectum
components.special_features: Final segment of digestive tract

digestive.digestive_process: Continuous grazing animal, stomach empties continuously into small intestine, needs frequent small meals

respiratory.description: Designed for efficient oxygen uptake during exercise
key_features: Obligate nasal breathers (cannot breathe through mouth)
Large lung capacity (55 liters at rest)
High respiratory rate (8-16 breaths per minute at rest, up to 180 during intense exercise)

components.name: Nostrils
components.special_features: Large, flaring capability to increase airflow during exercise

components.name: Nasal Passages
components.special_features: Complex turbinate bones increase surface area

components.name: Pharynx
components.special_features: Shared with digestive tract, soft palate separates mouth

components.name: Larynx
components.special_features: Contains vocal cords, subject to paralysis in some horses

components.name: Trachea
components.special_features: Rigid cartilage rings prevent collapse

components.name: Bronchi
components.special_features: Branch into smaller bronchioles

components.name: Lungs
components.special_features: Enormous surface area, takes up majority of thoracic cavity

components.name: Diaphragm
components.special_features: Dome-shaped, flattens during inhalation

respiratory.breathing_mechanism: Passive inhalation (diaphragm contraction creates negative pressure), active exhalation (abdominal muscle contraction)
respiratory.exercise_adaptation: Respiratory rate increases with exercise, 'synchronization' with stride at gallop

circulatory.description: Powerful system to support athletic performance
key_features: Low resting heart rate (28-44 beats per minute)
Can increase to 250 beats per minute during intense exercise
Total blood volume approximately 8-10% of body weight (80-100 liters in 1000kg horse)

components.name: Heart
components.special_features: Four-chambered, extremely efficient in athletic horses
components.variations: Racing breeds often have proportionally larger hearts

components.name: Arteries
components.special_features: Thick, elastic walls to handle pressure

components.name: Veins
components.special_features: Contain valves to prevent backflow, especially important in legs

components.name: Capillaries
components.function: Site of gas and nutrient exchange
components.special_features: Extremely numerous in muscle tissue

circulatory.spleen_function: Acts as blood reservoir, can contract during exercise to release additional red blood cells
circulatory.exercise_adaptation: Heart can increase output from 30 liters/min at rest to over 300 liters/min during exercise

nervous.description: Control system for body functions and behavior

components.name: Brain
components.special_features: Relatively small compared to body size, weighs approximately 1.5-2 pounds (650-900g)

components.name: Spinal Cord
components.function: Connects brain to body, controls reflexes
components.special_features: Protected by vertebral column, extends from brain to sacral region

components.name: Peripheral Nerves
components.function: Transmit signals between central nervous system and body
components.special_features: Complex network throughout body

sensory_systems.vision: Almost 360° field of view, motion sensitive, dichromatic color vision
sensory_systems.hearing: Mobile ears can locate sounds independently, sensitive to high frequencies
sensory_systems.touch: Highly sensitive, especially muzzle, flanks, and legs
sensory_systems.smell: Well-developed, important for social recognition and food selection
sensory_systems.taste: Selective grazers, can identify toxic plants

components.name: Testicles
components.special_features: Located in scrotum outside body cavity for temperature regulation

components.name: Penis
components.special_features: Retracted when not in use, contains erectile tissue

male.reproduction_capability: From 18-24 months to advanced age (20+ years)

components.name: Ovaries
components.special_features: Bean-shaped, contain follicles and corpus luteum

components.name: Oviducts
components.special_features: Connect ovaries to uterine horns

components.name: Uterus
components.special_features: Y-shaped with two horns and body

components.name: Cervix
components.special_features: Opens during estrus and birth, tightly closed during pregnancy

components.name: Vagina
components.special_features: Elastic to accommodate foal during birth

female.estrous_cycle: 21 days during breeding season (spring/summer), seasonal polyestrous

major_glands.name: Pituitary
major_glands.functions: Master gland controlling many other endocrine glands

immune.description: Defense system against disease and infection

components.name: Lymph Nodes
components.function: Filter lymph fluid, house immune cells
components.locations: Throughout body, especially under jaw, in front of shoulder, in groin

components.name: Spleen
components.special_features: Located behind stomach, also serves as blood reservoir

components.name: Thymus
components.special_features: Largest in young horses, shrinks with age

components.name: Tonsils
components.function: Defense against respiratory and digestive pathogens

immune.passive_immunity: Foals receive antibodies through colostrum (first milk)

components.name: Skin
components.special_features: Varies in thickness across body, thinnest on face and underside

components.name: Hair
components.seasonal_changes: Grows thicker winter coat, sheds in spring

components.name: Hooves
components.composition: Modified keratinized epidermis, similar to human fingernails

components.name: Chestnuts and Ergots
components.function: Vestigial structures, possibly remnants of scent glands
components.locations: Chestnuts on inside of legs, ergots behind fetlocks

components.name: Sweat Glands
components.special_features: Distributed throughout skin, produce protein-rich sweat

embryonic.description: Development from conception to differentiation of major body systems
key_developments: Day 1-5: Fertilized egg divides and moves through oviduct to uterus
Day 6-15: Embryo floats freely in uterus
Day 16-22: Embryo attaches to uterine wall
Day 22-40: Formation of primitive organ systems, recognizable as horse embryo
Month 2: All organ systems present in primitive form
Month 3-4: Rapid growth, hardening of bones, growth of fetlocks
Month 5-7: Growth of hair, development of muscles
Month 8-11: Continued growth and maturation of all systems, positioning for birth
fetal.size_progression: Growth from few centimeters to approximately 100-120 cm (40-48 inches) at birth

characteristics: Long legs relative to body depth
Proportionally large head and short neck
Rapid growth, gaining 2-3 pounds per day initially
Primary dentition (deciduous teeth)
Able to stand within 1-2 hours of birth
Able to run within 24 hours
developmental_milestones: Birth-24 hours: Standing, nursing, bonding with mother
1-4 weeks: Exploring environment, playful behavior, sampling solid food
1-3 months: Increasing independence, more social play with other foals
4-6 months: Preparing for weaning, consuming significant solid food
foal.anatomical_notes: Epiphyseal growth plates very active, susceptible to developmental orthopedic diseases

characteristics: More balanced proportions but still growing
Continued growth of body catching up to legs
Beginning to lose deciduous teeth
Becoming more independent socially
weanling.growth_rate: Slows to approximately 1-1.5 pounds per day
weanling.critical_developments: Continued bone development, important nutritional period for future soundness

characteristics: Significant growth, approaching 90% of adult height
Adolescent appearance, still developing muscle definition
Sexual maturation beginning (especially fillies)
Continued replacement of deciduous teeth with permanent teeth
yearling.growth_patterns: Growth spurts common, often appearing awkward or unbalanced during growth phases

characteristics: Near adult height but still filling out
Increasing muscle development
Most permanent teeth erupted (except canines and last molars)
Sexual maturity in most individuals
two_year_old.anatomical_notes: Most growth plates closing, but some important ones (vertebral bodies, femoral head) still active

characteristics: Full physical development
Maximum strength and athletic capability
All permanent teeth present and functional
Complete closure of growth plates
mature.anatomical_notes: Dental changes continue throughout life with wear patterns developing

characteristics: May show signs of aging (gray hairs, especially around eyes and muzzle)
Changes in body condition (more angular appearance, potential weight loss)
Wear on teeth becoming significant
Potential joint changes affecting movement
senior.variations: Aging rate varies greatly with genetics, use, and care throughout life
senior.anatomical_notes: Changes in digestive efficiency, dental wear affecting nutrition, potential joint degeneration

adaptations.advantage: Increases speed, efficiency of movement, reduces weight at end of limb
Standing with minimal muscle fatigue, efficient long-distance travel
Energy conservation during movement, spring-like quality
Selective grazing, efficient gathering of grass
Withstand abrasive plant material, continual eruption compensates for wear
Able to extract nutrients from fibrous plants unsuitable for other animals
Can remain alert while head down grazing

environmental.description: Adaptations to survive in natural environments

adaptations.advantage: Adaptation to various climates through sweating, coat changes
Adapted to various terrains, natural hoof maintenance through movement
